# Artifact Keeper 1.10.0

A large, broad release — 232 items closed in the milestone, roughly twice the size of 1.9.0. The headline additions are a server-side container image builder and inspector (#4034), an ingestion seam that lets any out-of-tree scanner feed the policy gates that already exist (#3411), and upstream authentication to Amazon ECR and AWS CodeArtifact with tokens the server mints and refreshes itself (#1559); the bulk of the rest is proxy, format and storage-accounting correctness. Sixteen security fixes ship with it, and a handful of deliberate refusals change behaviour you may be relying on — read the numbered sections before you deploy.

Ten migrations run on start-up (210, 212, 214 through 221). All are additive and none of them blocks reads or writes, but migration 215 is a full-table aggregate over both proxy tables inside its own transaction: on an instance with a busy proxy and a long retention window, budget seconds to minutes of extra start-up time on the upgrade that applies it (#3577). Two subsystems additionally need an admin call once the migrations finish.

## Read this first — storage GC refuses any request that does not say `dry_run`

**`POST /api/v1/admin/storage-gc` and `POST /api/v1/repositories/{key}/storage-gc` now require `dry_run` in the body and reject unknown fields, answering `422` and deleting nothing** (#3501). Both endpoints delete irreversibly, and `dry_run` was optional and defaulted to `false` — so an empty `{}` meant "really delete", and so did every misspelling of the one field that could have said otherwise (`dryRun`, `dry_Run`, `dryrun`). During 1.8.2 verification a typo'd key deleted a batch of attribution rows exactly that way. Rejecting was chosen over flipping the default so that the break is loud and happens once.

Any automation posting an empty or field-less body must now send `{"dry_run": false}` explicitly to keep performing live GC; it will receive `422` until it does, and nothing will have been deleted in the meantime. One first-party caller breaks: `ak admin storage-gc run` without `--dry-run` builds its body as `{}` and needs a CLI release before it can run a live pass again (`--dry-run` keeps working). The web UI's storage panel already sends the field and is unaffected.

## Read this second — two backfills and one SQL fix to run after upgrading

**Run `POST /api/v1/admin/packages/backfill` once** (#3659, #3660). Fifteen hosted format handlers — alpine, cargo, chef, cocoapods, conda, goproxy, huggingface, jetbrains, protobuf, pub, rpm, sbt, swift, terraform and vscode — wrote their `artifacts` row and never registered the package, so those uploads were visible under Artifacts and absent from Packages. New publishes register from this release on; the admin endpoint replays existing live artifacts through the same upsert, is idempotent and safe to re-run, and returns what it scanned, registered, skipped and failed. It is synchronous and does its work in the request, so pick a quiet window on a large instance. The same change also stops a catalog row whose artifacts are all gone from haunting the Packages page.

**Run `POST /api/v1/admin/storage/ledger/backfill` only if this database was ever restored from a backup** (#3650). `total_storage_bytes` sums `repository_usage_ledger`, which is maintained exclusively by migration 182's row-level triggers — and a restore inserts rows rather than writing them through the application, so the headline reflected only what the instance had written since the restore. The endpoint is an absolute recompute from the authoritative tables, so it is idempotent and reports zero drift on a healthy instance. It is safe to run GC before it; neither GC orphan rule reads the ledger.

**NuGet instances need one SQL run** (#3976). A push registered the catalog row twice — once under the `.nuspec` casing and once lowercased — so `FiscalTapeParser.Xml` came with a metadata-less `fiscaltapeparser.xml` twin. New pushes write one row; rows already created keep showing until they are merged, and #3976 carries the idempotent SQL that folds each lowercased twin's `package_versions` into the row that kept the published casing and deletes the twin.

## Read this third — anonymous `/v2` pulls stop working where guest access is off

**`AK_GUEST_ACCESS_ENABLED=false` now applies to the OCI Distribution surface** (#3854). The guest-access guard allowlisted the whole `/v2` subtree, so the server-wide anonymous policy was never asked on manifest, blob, tag or referrer paths; the OCI handlers then asked only whether the *repository* was anonymously readable. An unauthenticated `docker pull` of a `public` repository therefore succeeded on an instance that had turned guest access off, with nothing in the logs.

On instances running the default (`true`) nothing changes. Where the flag is off, the repositories that lose anonymous pulls are exactly those that were `public` before the flag was set, since the API already coerces a new `public` request to `private` while it is off. Stored visibility is untouched and re-enabling the flag restores exactly what it withheld. The refusal is now the distribution spec's error envelope with a `Bearer` challenge pointing at `/v2/token`, so a container client renders an error instead of hanging on a realm it cannot use; `docker login` and every pull made with the credential it leaves behind are unaffected, which is the fix for a pipeline that breaks.

## Read this fourth — Swagger UI is opt-in, and the break-glass flag goes admin-only

**`GET /swagger-ui/` and `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` are mounted only when `ENABLE_SWAGGER=true`** (#3489). They were previously mounted whenever `ENVIRONMENT` was not `production`, and the code default is `development` — so any deployment that never set the variable served a complete, unauthenticated map of every route, parameter and schema to anonymous callers, and `ENABLE_SWAGGER=false` turned them on too, because the check was presence-only. `ENVIRONMENT` no longer affects either surface. Anyone reaching `/swagger-ui/` today without the flag gets a `404` after upgrading; set `ENABLE_SWAGGER=true` on that instance to restore it. Spec export, SDK generation and the CI `openapi.json` artifact are untouched.

Separately, `auth.admin_break_glass_enabled` is removed from the anonymous `GET /api/v1/system/config` and joins the admin-only tier. It told an unauthenticated caller whether a local admin password path into the instance exists, which is precisely the reconnaissance wanted before probing the login route. No shipped client reads it — the login page decides from `local_login_enabled`, and `?fallback=local` remains the admin recovery route. The rest of the pre-authentication `auth` block is unchanged.

## Read this fifth — scans that reported zero findings start reporting real ones

**Hosted PyPI sdists, RubyGems, Cargo and NuGet uploads are graded instead of being persisted as clean scans of nothing** (#3603). The hosted-upload path extracts into a workspace and runs the CVE engine in directory mode, and directory cataloging reads a fixed set of ecosystem layouts that none of these four formats actually publish — so the engine cataloged nothing, matched nothing, and the scan was stored `completed` with `findings_count = 0`, indistinguishable from clean. Any severity gate or quarantine policy configured for those formats was a no-op on that path. Each now carries a pin the engine can grade: measured against a current database, `rack@2.0.7` goes from 0 findings to 35, and `PyYAML@5.3.1`, `smallvec@1.6.0` and `Newtonsoft.Json@12.0.1` each from 0 to 1. Wheels are unchanged (they already catalog themselves); the `chocolatey` and `powershell` aliases come along with NuGet.

**Conda packages are unpacked into the scan workspace at all** (#4035). Neither container was recognised, and the extractor had no bzip2 or zstd branch, so a `.conda` or `.tar.bz2` was handed to the engine as a single unreadable blob — the scan ran, cataloged nothing and reported zero findings. Both containers are now extracted in-process under the existing traversal, entry-count and byte ceilings, threaded as one budget so nesting cannot multiply the cap.

In both cases existing `scan_results` rows are not rewritten: the new verdict appears on the next scan. Previously-passing gates will begin to block artifacts that were always vulnerable, and anything promoted or released under a zero-finding result on these formats should be rescanned deliberately rather than assumed clean.

## Read this sixth — smaller refusals and shape changes

- **Quarantine can no longer be enabled on a Remote or Virtual repository** (#3647); `PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` answers `400`. Quarantine state lives on `artifacts`, which a proxying repository has none of, so the policy was a total block with no release path and no age awareness. Repositories that already have it on are left exactly as set and warned about at start-up and on every API read — turn it off with `{"quarantine_enabled": false}` and enable the policy on the hosted repository the content lands in.
- **SBOM mutations require the repository `write`/`delete` action, not read visibility** (#3824, GHSA-ww52-pmcg-f53c). Members whose role lacks `delete` can no longer delete an SBOM, and non-members can no longer generate or convert one on a public repository. And **lifecycle policy create and update now reject an unrecognised `config` key with `422`** (#2024) instead of ignoring it, so a misspelled exclusion block cannot silently delete what it was written to protect. Validation runs on create and update only; a policy already stored with a stray key keeps running.
- **`GET /api/v1/peers/{id}/repositories` returns full subscription objects, not bare UUIDs** (#3575). A client reading a flat array of strings must now read `.repository_id` from each element; the rows, ids and order are otherwise identical. Regenerate any SDK from the published spec.
- **A Maven PUT of a resolved unique snapshot answers `409`** (#3839). The upload path now takes mutability from the same classifier the cache uses, so a timestamped snapshot leaf can no longer be silently overwritten. Non-unique snapshots still republish in place.
- **Scan-on-proxy actually gates VSIX delivery on `vscode` remotes** (#3254, #3255, #3256). A repository with `scan_on_proxy` already enabled was serving proxied extension packages unscanned; after upgrading those pulls are gated, and under `fail_closed` an inconclusive scan answers `423` rather than serving. An unrecognised `targetPlatform` is now a `400`.
- **Token exchanges return shorter-lived bearers** (#3460, #3625, #3548, #3820). See the Security section: nothing that worked stops working, but a client that hardcodes a 30-minute refresh interval will start seeing `401`s.
- **Swift releases and JetBrains plugins published through the multipart paths are corrupt on disk and must be republished** (#3595, #3848) — the stored bytes were the multipart envelope, or a lossy UTF-8 copy, and the recorded checksum describes the corruption, so nothing detects it automatically. Unrelatedly, **the Windows release asset is now a `.zip`** (#3637): `artifact-keeper-windows-amd64.exe` is now `artifact-keeper-windows-amd64.zip` with the binary inside it; installers pinned to the `.exe` URL must unzip. The four Unix targets are unchanged.

## Security

Sixteen fixes, grouped by what they close. The fourth class, scanning coverage (#3603, #4035), is described above; the rest:

- **Auth, session and access control.** Anonymous `/v2` pulls now honour the server-wide guest-access policy (#3854). Four credential-exchange endpoints — the three OCI `/v2/token` arms and Conan `users/authenticate` — minted a full-lifetime JWT regardless of how little life the presented credential had left, and the Conan JWT is itself a valid credential for that same endpoint, so re-presenting each bearer before it expired was a self-sustaining renewal chain that outlived the API token, its rotation and any configured maximum; all four now cap the mint at the presenting credential's own expiry (#3460, #3625), as does the CI token exchange (#3548, #3820). `/api/v1/auth/logout` never revoked anything — it was mounted without the optional-auth middleware, so the revocation branch and the audit entry were dead code and a captured 7-day refresh token stayed usable after logout (#3824, GHSA-965p-gcgh-67vf). SBOM mutations moved behind the write and delete actions (#3824, GHSA-ww52-pmcg-f53c). Webhook reads now honour an API token's repository scope, so a token minted for one repository can no longer list another's webhook URLs, headers, secret digests and delivery history (#3715) — token confinement, not privilege escalation.
- **Oracles and error leaks.** The repository-visibility middleware cached only rows that matched, so a repeated probe of an existing out-of-scope key answered from memory in ~40 µs while a nonexistent key re-ran the query at ~350 µs — the last discriminator left after 1.9.0 made the wire answers byte-identical; a confirmed miss is now cached under the same window, with eviction on create, rename and delete across replicas (#3750). The `/v2` repository resolver built its error envelope from the driver's own text, so an anonymous `docker pull` against a saturated pool or a broken schema was answered with the pool state or the table name (#3761). 1.9.0's sweep gated one phrasing; the same class survived under three others across eighteen native formats — 35 `Storage error` sites rendering the internal storage key and the OS error, the hex signing-key lookups, and 33 sites carrying an `io::Error`, a signing failure or a `reqwest` error naming the configured upstream (#3718). Status codes and envelopes are unchanged; only the message text moves, so anything scraping that detail off a 500 must read the server log instead. Swagger UI, the OpenAPI document and the break-glass advertisement are covered above (#3489).
- **Ingestion validation.** `validate_artifact_path` was wired only into the generic REST upload, so thirteen native write paths — terraform, cargo, helm, pypi, npm, goproxy, nuget, cran, composer, rubygems, jetbrains, conan and ansible — accepted and stored names, versions and filenames containing `..`, `//`, backslashes, NULs or percent-encoded variants; every cited path now validates at ingest and rejects with `400`, and Conan's `%2e%2f` bypass and a lone encoded dot are closed with it (#3824, GHSA-vcq6-8hxw-4q67). HuggingFace's `x-filename` header was spliced verbatim into the artifact path and storage key, so `../../evil.bin` overwrote another file on the filesystem backend; it is now rejected rather than sanitised (#3824, GHSA-6wjw-gcvx-3q58).
- **Dependency CVEs.** `cryptoki` 0.12.0 to 0.12.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0286 (GHSA-r6vc-97x9-63vv), where the PKCS 11 client read an attribute's byte length as an element count and could build an out-of-bounds slice — lockfile-only, and inert without an HSM. `rustls` 0.23.43 to 0.23.45 for RUSTSEC-2026-0285 (#3878), TLS 1.3 handshake messages accepted across encryption-level boundaries; `rustls` is the TLS stack under every outbound connection the registry makes. And CVE-2026-84445 in gRPC-Go, which had failed the Docker Publish security scan on every `main` build since 2026-09-09 without a byte of the repository changing: the backend's bundled grype moves its grpc override to v1.83.2 (#3790, #3792) and the scanner adapter is rebuilt on hardened trivy 0.74.0-r3 and published as 1.2.11 (#3790). The vulnerable path is an xDS server; neither binary serves anything, so the flaw was never reachable here — it is built rather than suppressed because that is the rule for a dependency CVE with a version to build against.

## Proxy and virtual repositories

- A concurrent cold fetch of a large proxied artifact could hand every waiting client a body that stopped mid-download under a `200` with a full `Content-Length` (#3363). Followers of a single-flighted miss were dropped from a lossy broadcast channel and then yielded an error into a response whose status was already on the wire; in the first multi-replica concurrency run, 198 of 200 clients received the same 2.9 MB prefix of a 256 MiB artifact, and nothing was logged. A follower's outcome is now decided before it is handed a body, and a late arrival waits for the leader instead of returning instantly and cold-fetching upstream itself — which is how one cold object became 38 upstream fetches in that same run.
- Cache entries are classified against the repository's real format again (#3556): the synthesized upstream repository hardcoded `Generic`, which has no classifier, so version-pinned RPMs, createrepo primaries, conda packages, digest-addressed layers staged for the inline image scan and everything fetched through the generic download route fell to the conservative five-minute mutable default and were re-fetched from upstream forever. Two negative-caching corrections sit alongside it: an upstream `410 Gone` during revalidation is negative-cached like a `404` instead of pinning the stale copy indefinitely with no revalidation that could ever correct it (#3749), and the OCI virtual resolver no longer records a throttled or failing member as "this does not exist" — a negative is written only when every member gave a definitive answer (#3836). The virtual negative cache's window and size are now operator-configurable within clamped bounds, with byte-identical defaults (#1424).
- A tagged image pulled through an OCI Virtual repository reaches the packages catalog for the request shape Docker and containerd actually issue — `HEAD` by tag, then `GET` by digest — where the catalog write previously never ran (#3602). Ownership stays with the resolving member, so the same image behind several Virtuals produces one set of rows. And OCI and Docker blob `GET` now honours a single `Range` request across hosted, virtual and pull-through paths (#3586), so an interrupted layer download can resume instead of restarting. Cold-cache streaming still tees the complete object into the cache; only the client-facing stream is sliced.
- `npm audit signatures` sent every attestation lookup upstream on every call, with no cache read, write or TTL; in one observed day those lookups were 17.8% of all requests and 94% of all 404s, at ~67 identical questions per distinct URI (#3764). A deliberately narrow negative cache now fronts them — attestation paths only, negative answers only, keyed on the answering member — governed by `NPM_ATTESTATION_NEGATIVE_CACHE_TTL_SECS` (default 3600).

## Scanning and findings

An out-of-tree scanner can now post a batch of findings for an artifact through `POST /api/v1/security/findings/external`, and they feed the same download gates, artifact scores and promotion gates the in-tree adapters do (#3411). The row is written already `completed` rather than `pending`, deliberately — a parked row would trip `block_unscanned` into a permanent false block that no janitor would reap — and the endpoint requires admin plus a dedicated `write:findings` scope, so a credential that may publish packages cannot also write the verdicts the gates read. The scan type is the generic `external` (migration 220, applied in the online shape), with the vendor recorded in `source` and `scanner_version`.

`GET /security/scans` accepts a `scan_type` filter and a scan's findings accept `severity`, `source` and `cve_id` (#3410); unknown values are rejected with a `400` naming the accepted set rather than returning an unfiltered page that reads as "no findings match". A proxied download with scan-on-proxy enabled no longer re-runs the full inline scan on every fetch of the same bytes — the freshness token recorded whichever applicable scanner answered first, which on any deployment with the Trivy filesystem scanner wired was Trivy, stored under `scan_type = 'grype'` and never matched again, costing ~7 s and a 504 per request (#4019). The first pull after upgrading re-scans once, then the stored verdict is reused. `INCUS_SCANNER_ENABLED=false` now keeps the Incus scanner out of the registry entirely (#3874), and Cargo dependency scanning works again after a `toml` 1.0 parser change made every `Cargo.toml` report zero dependencies with nothing in the logs (#3699, #3690).

## Formats

- **PyPI and Jupyter.** PyPI repositories serve the legacy JSON API and XML-RPC `browse`, so JupyterLab 4's Extension Manager works against a private index instead of being disabled or pointed at pypi.org (#3783); `jupyter` joins `poetry` and `conda` as a PyPI alias format on the same routes (#3784, migration 212). Curation now runs for `poetry`, `jupyter`, `yarn` and `pnpm` staging repositories, whose pending rows previously stayed pending forever (#3787).
- **Cargo and Maven.** A Cargo Remote can hold newly published crate versions behind the same publish-age gate npm, PyPI and VS Code already use, closing the fast-burn window the 2026-08-20 `arrayref`/`append-only-vec` compromise ran in (#3480, contributed by @cazlo in #3483). Both the sparse index and the direct `.crate` download are gated, because either alone is bypassable. On the Maven side, concurrent uploads of one path no longer surface a unique-constraint violation as a `500` on an ordinary snapshot republish (#3587), and snapshot mutability comes from the classifier (#3839).
- **NuGet.** A virtual repository federates its members instead of letting one half hide the other: downloads walk members in declared order rather than always asking remotes first, and the version list and registration index merge upstream with local instead of consulting upstream only when the local result is empty — which had made `dotnet restore` fail with NU1102 for every version of any id the private repository also published (#3980).
- **Go.** A virtual repository's `@v/list` collates every member the caller may read, so publishing one hotfix build to a hosted member no longer erases the upstream's entire version history (#833). This widens the listing, not what the repository serves; precedence is unchanged, and members that error or time out are skipped and logged.
- **Helm, Debian and RPM.** A Helm Remote no longer doubles its upstream's subpath when the upstream index advertises root-relative chart URLs, which had 404'd every chart download from another Artifact Keeper instance (#3705) — the consumption half of 1.9.0's #3680. A Debian remote streams `.deb` content published under `dists/` instead of buffering it and answering `502` past the 128 MiB metadata ceiling, which vendor mirrors such as Proxmox hit (#3596); RPM repodata is streamed rather than buffered, so there is no ceiling left for a large `primary.xml.gz` to outgrow (#3486, #2622).
- **Swift, JetBrains, Terraform, Ansible.** Swift publishes store the `source-archive` part rather than the whole multipart envelope, and no longer buffer the upload (#3595). JetBrains multipart publishes are parsed on bytes instead of a lossy UTF-8 copy, which had panicked the request or stored corruption whose SHA-256 matched the corruption (#3848). An authenticated Terraform mirror hands out ticketed archive URLs, since Terraform does not send credentials for the archives it is told about (#3588). A hosted Ansible collection advertises the dependency map from its own `MANIFEST.json` instead of reporting none (#3600); collections published earlier must be re-published. Separately, the web UI's own artifact upload is no longer refused with the CSRF header error, which had blocked the one operation the upload tab exists for (#3592).

## Auth and SSO

A SAML configuration can be addressed by an operator-chosen `slug`, so rebuilding a deployment no longer mints a new UUID and forces the ACS URL to be re-pasted at the identity provider (#2583, migration 218). Nothing existing changes: the migration backfills nothing, every configuration keeps its current URL until an operator sets a slug, and both forms resolve for as long as you need them to. Remote repositories can authenticate to Amazon ECR and AWS CodeArtifact through the process's own AWS identity, with the minted token cached, re-minted before expiry, never persisted and never rendered (#1559); the recommended Kubernetes deployment stores no AWS secret at all. The keyless CI token exchange resolves its provider from the assertion's own `iss` instead of requiring a `provider_id` that only an admin-only endpoint published — the "no static secrets" flow had begun by using the most privileged credential in the system (#3548); `provider_id` stays accepted.

Administrators can require newly minted API tokens to expire, bound the range and default an omitted expiry (#3460, #3625, migration 216). Enforcement is mint-time only: migration 216 seeds `require_expiration: false`, which is exactly the historical behaviour, tokens already in the table keep whatever expiry they were minted with and continue to authenticate, and a client that omits `expires_in_days` is defaulted rather than refused. The policy endpoint reports how many live never-expiring tokens exist, split by holder, so they can be rotated deliberately. The per-boot OIDC reconcile keeps `attribute_mapping` keys the environment never set instead of erasing them on every restart, which had silently undone the documented remedy for an IdP publishing groups under a non-default claim (#3507); `OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP` stays env-definitive. A first federated or CI login no longer hands back an access token that its own privilege-change watermark has already invalidated (#3946).

## Storage and lifecycle

Lifecycle policies accept an `exclude` block naming versions and version patterns they must never delete, compiled into both the candidate query and the soft-delete so an excluded artifact is never selected rather than selected and spared (#2024, migration 217); a dry run now reports `bytes_matched`, which there was previously nowhere to report. OCI objects orphaned by a repository delete are reclaimed instead of leaking forever — the delete cascaded away exactly the rows GC scans from, so an object became undiscoverable at the instant it became reclaimable; the keys are now recorded in a durable candidate set before the cascade and swept afterwards, behind the same 24-hour grace window blob GC uses (#3733, migration 219). Deleting a repository while the GC tick or the stats recompute runs no longer deadlocks (#4004), and the recompute tolerates a repository vanishing mid-run in both places the foreign key can catch it (#3957). Proxy-cached objects are counted in the per-repository storage breakdown and the daily snapshot, where a pull-through repository serving terabytes had read as empty (#3577, migration 210, backfilled as a lower bound by migration 215), and proxy cache hits are recorded for fourteen formats that served them and counted neither (#3649) — the counters will step up, which is a measurement correction and not new traffic.

Alibaba Cloud OSS works as a backend for the first time. Every `ListObjectsV2` failed to parse, so browse, the storage tree and proxy-cache enumeration all read as empty while direct reads and writes worked (#3593), and every OCI blob commit `500`'d because the rename is a `CopyObject` that OSS answers only under its own header (#3594). Both are handled in the backend with automatic endpoint detection and an optional `S3_PROVIDER` override; no existing deployment changes behaviour.

## Operations

`OPENSEARCH_INDEX_PREFIX` lets more than one instance share an OpenSearch cluster, where the index names were bare constants and two instances read and wrote each other's documents (#3669); the variable is empty by default and an unset prefix resolves to exactly the historical names, and setting it on an existing deployment points that instance at a new empty index that the existing bootstrap path repopulates in the background. `/search/quick` finally queries OpenSearch when it is configured, instead of an index being written and never read (#3670) — visibility is enforced from PostgreSQL on every hit, never from the index's own stale `is_public` flag, and any cluster failure falls back to the PostgreSQL path. The first-boot admin password can be preset from `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` or, preferably, `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE`, so an unattended deployment never has to `exec` into the container to read a generated password (#2803); it applies only while the admin account is being created.

A custom `S3_ENDPOINT` on AWS no longer refuses to start without static keys (#4060). The startup gate read every custom endpoint — an S3 VPC endpoint, a FIPS endpoint, a non-commercial partition — as definitively not AWS, so an airgapped EC2 deployment died at boot with no way forward short of minting long-lived keys. Before returning that error the backend now makes one IMDSv2 request under a one-second budget with no retries, and boots on the instance profile if it answers; `S3_USE_INSTANCE_PROFILE=true` is the explicit opt-in where the probe cannot see, and `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true` restores the previous error verbatim. MinIO, Ceph RGW and friends have nothing on that address, fail in milliseconds and still get the original fail-fast error.

The backend and openscap images run under OpenShift's `restricted-v2` SCC as an arbitrary high UID, where every write previously failed before the first request was served (#3434); the scanner-adapter image is not yet converted, so an end-to-end deployment on `restricted-v2` still needs Phase 2. Release binaries are about 15% smaller (#3637). A migration no longer re-walks its Nexus source once per page, which made runtime super-linear in component count and a large repository indistinguishable from a hang, and a finished job's counters and report now describe what it really did rather than a single run's bytes (#3590, #3512); a cancelled migration is logged as cancelled instead of as a pause (#3498); and a migrated generic or raw artifact keeps its source path instead of being filed under a second copy of the repository key (#3654) — re-running the migration repairs a repository imported before the fix, and its doubled download URLs will `404` afterwards by design.

## Other fixes worth knowing

- `artifact.uploaded` and `artifact.deleted` webhooks and email subscriptions had never fired for anyone: they were mapped, subscribable and documented, with no producer anywhere (#3411). They now fire from the shared service choke points, and from the shared catalog registration every native publish makes — so `cargo publish`, `npm publish`, `helm push` and `docker push` deliver too (#3411 follow-up). A cache fill is not an upload and stays silent.
- Virtual repositories aggregate their members' content in the Packages page and the Docker grouped tag view, which filtered by the virtual repository's own key and so came back empty while the flat listing showed the same content (#3532).
- A proxied multi-arch tag's catalog size is the image size rather than `0` or a few kilobytes of manifest JSON (#3601). There is no backfill; a warm cached tag keeps its row until it is re-fetched. Separately, a `HEAD` on an uncached remote OCI blob larger than 8 MiB reported `404` while the matching `GET` returned `200`, so clients that head before pulling saw large layers as missing (#3605).
- The scheduled storage-GC tick's singleton lease covered only the first of its four workloads, so blob GC and the stats recompute ran on every replica at every occurrence (#3503), and a job that lost its lease mid-run kept working against a lease another replica now held (#3502).
- A Nexus migration no longer fails a large transfer on the clock or a whole item on a transient source blip, and the source URL is redacted before a retry warning is logged (#3569). And completing a chunked upload no longer rewrites a content-addressed object that is already stored; the filesystem backend's `put_file` was also the one write in that backend that was not stage-and-rename, so an interrupted copy could leave a truncated object under a content-addressed key (#3517, #3530).

## Added

Beyond the image builder, the external findings seam and the AWS upstream auth types described above, this release adds a CI gate that fails any new migration which would block writes on a hot table, together with `docs/operations/online-migrations.md` — the runbook for the five online rewrites that replace them (#3864, #2524). Nothing changes at runtime and no existing migration is edited; the audit's 47 grandfathered statements go on an exact allowlist, so both a new offender and a stale entry fail the build. Every published release digest is now verified after the fact for a build-provenance attestation and a cosign signature, and the check can be rehearsed against an already-published tag in passing and refusing scenarios (#3519). A patch release can be cut from a `release/X.Y.x` maintenance branch through the certified-candidate flow without widening the Sigstore identity the verifier pins (#3769, #3771, #3772, #2983), and the release-branch gate and release preflight now apply one shared exemption set instead of disagreeing about which commits are acceptable (#3829).

## Web UI

`artifact-keeper-web` 1.10.0 is the matching front end for this release and should be deployed with it. It adds the token expiration policy panel, lifecycle policy exclusions, the SAML slug field, the AWS upstream authentication types, the external scan type and finding filters and a maintenance card, and changes the age-policy panel to match the backend.
